title: Accelerated Manager Activation Framework
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Summary:
This document defines the Accelerated Manager Activation Framework (AMAF): a repeatable, measurable onboarding and certification path for newly promoted or newly hired people managers at Redwood Inference. AMAF is designed to reduce time-to-impact, align expectations with business goals, and provide a clear escalation and sponsor model for the first 120 days.

Audience:
- New managers (individual contributors promoted into manager roles or external hires with direct reports)
- Their skip-levels and onboarding sponsors
- People Ops and Leadership Development partners

Goals and success metrics:
- Achieve role-certification within 120 days for 85% of participants.
- Manager ramp score (composite of direct-report feedback, 1:1 cadence adherence, and operational milestones) >= 75 by day 120.
- Reduce time-to-stable-team-performance (measured by team health index) by 20% vs. legacy baseline.

Overview and principles:
- Sponsor-led: every new manager is paired with a senior sponsor (peer manager or director) for the first 120 days. The sponsor provides tactical support, shadowing sessions, and rollout approvals.
- Outcome-oriented: focus on concrete operational outcomes (OKR alignment, hiring plan, performance calibrations) rather than just orientation content.
- Lightweight certification gates: explicit milestone checks at Day 30, Day 60, Day 90, and Day 120.
- Asynchronous-friendly: most check-ins and knowledge transfer are supported with templates and recorded sessions to accommodate distributed teams.

Roles and responsibilities:
- New manager: complete checklists, schedule required meetings, run initial 1:1s, present team plan at Day 30 and Day 90 checkpoints.
- Sponsor: weekly office hours, counter-sign key decisions (hiring plan, performance warnings), provide feedback for certification gates.
- People Ops partner: run cohort orientation, provide manager toolkit and training bookings, track milestone completion in HRIS.
- Skip-level (manager's manager): sets success criteria and approves final certification.

Activation timeline and checkpoints (high level):
1) Pre-boarding (Offer -> Day 0)
   - Deliver manager welcome packet and role expectations doc.
   - Assign sponsor and People Ops contact.
   - Shared calendar invites: orientation, 1:1 coach, functional training.
2) Day 0 -> Day 30 (Stability & Listening)
   - Objectives: complete people inventory, hold 1:1s with direct reports, produce a 30-day team plan.
   - Deliverables: 30-day team plan (slides or doc), initial hiring triage, one operational quick-win identified.
   - Gate: Sponsor review of 30-day plan; if issues flagged, run an aligned remediation plan (see Remediation section).
3) Day 31 -> Day 60 (Operationalizing)
   - Objectives: implement quick-win, finalize hiring priorities, set team-level OKRs, run first coaching cycle.
   - Deliverables: hiring pipeline plan, team OKR draft, coaching rubric applied to at least one direct report.
   - Gate: People Ops validates completion of core trainings (Harassment Prevention, Security Basics, Manager Foundations).
4) Day 61 -> Day 90 (Performance & Culture)
   - Objectives: run the first performance calibration for the team, complete 90-day skip-level review, show evidence of 1:1 routines and feedback practice.
   - Deliverables: calibration notes, team health pulse, 90-day retrospective with action items.
   - Gate: Sponsor and skip-level sign-off on readiness to lead independently.
5) Day 91 -> Day 120 (Certification & Handover)
   - Objectives: confirm hiring commitments, complete final certification packet, schedule handoff to People Ops for long-term development plan.
   - Deliverables: certification packet, development plan, 120-day retrospective.
   - Gate: Final certification decision recorded in HRIS; badge awarded (Manager: Activated).

Checklists (copy-and-use templates)
- Pre-boarding checklist:
  - [ ] Manager welcome packet sent
  - [ ] Sponsor assigned
  - [ ] Key systems access requested (Slack, HRIS, OKR tool, Console)
  - [ ] Initial calendar: orientation, 1:1s, product walkthrough

- Day 0-30 checklist:
  - [ ] People inventory completed
  - [ ] 1:1s scheduled with all direct reports weekly
  - [ ] 30-day team plan submitted to sponsor
  - [ ] Completed security basics training

- Day 31-60 checklist:
  - [ ] Hiring priority list & job reqs drafted
  - [ ] Team OKRs drafted and reviewed
  - [ ] At least one coaching session observed by sponsor

- Day 61-120 checklist:
  - [ ] Performance calibration notes submitted
  - [ ] Development plan created for each direct report
  - [ ] Certification packet complete and signed

Certification packet contents (table):
| Item | Owner | Evidence format | Required by |
| Role success criteria | Skip-level | Written acceptance of criteria | Day 30 |
| 30/60/90 deliverables | Manager | Docs/slides | Day 90 |
| Training completion | People Ops | HRIS transcript | Day 60 |
| Sponsor feedback form | Sponsor | Signed form | Day 90 |
| Team health pulse | Manager | Pulse survey results | Day 90 |

Remediation and escalation protocol:
1. If a gate is failed, sponsor opens a Remediation Plan (RP) with 30-day measurable outcomes.
2. RP owner is the manager; sponsor monitors weekly and logs progress to People Ops.
3. If RP does not meet criteria after 30 days, skip-level initiates a formal coaching track or role reassessment.

Manager toolkit (links and templates):
- Weekly 1:1 agenda (template)
- Direct report onboarding checklist
- Hiring scorecard template (must include competencies, work sample rubric, and culture fit notes)
- Coaching observation rubric

Sample: Weekly 1:1 agenda template (copy)
1. Quick personal check-in (2–3m)
2. Wins since last time (5m)
3. Top priorities & blockers (10m)
4. Development conversation (10m)
5. Action items and commitments (3m)

Hiring scorecard quick reference:
- Technical competency (1–5)
- Role scope fit (1–5)
- Communication & collaboration (1–5)
- Cultural fit with Redwood values (1–5)
- Overall hire recommendation (yes/no/maybe)

Operational integrations and tracking:
- People Ops will track milestone completion in HRIS and attach certification packets to the manager profile.
- Managers should update a shared activation Trello/board with weekly progress; sponsor and People Ops have edit access.
- Standard pulse survey will run Day 60 and Day 90 to capture team health; results feed into the certification packet.

Training and learning sequence (required within first 60 days):
- Manager Foundations (live cohort)
- Psychological Safety & Feedback Lab (recorded + live practice)
- Performance Calibration Workshop
- Security & Data Handling for Managers

Examples and templates (inline):
- Sample 30-day plan header:
  - Team context (2–3 lines)
  - Immediate risks (3 bullets)
  - Top 3 objectives for next 30 days
  - Hiring priorities (top 2 roles)
  - Quick-win timeline (owner and dates)

- Sample sponsor feedback form (fields):
  - Readiness summary (text)
  - Strengths observed (bullets)
  - Areas for immediate focus (bullets)
  - Recommendation (proceed/remediate/reassess)

Operational notes and boundaries:
- Certification is not promotion; it is a measure of readiness to operate the manager role independently.
- Confidential performance issues must be handled via People Ops with HR guidance; do not discuss disciplinary details in open documents.

Rollout plan for company adoption:
1. Pilot cohort: Q4 2024, 12 managers across Eng and Product.
2. Measure outcomes (cert rate, team pulse delta, hiring velocity) over 6 months.
3. Iterate toolkit and automated HRIS flows based on cohort feedback.

Ownership and maintenance:
- Document owner: People Ops (Marisol Chen)
- Review cadence: annual or after each pilot (whichever sooner)
- Escalation contact: Head of People Ops (Priya Rao).

Related resources:
- /confluence/people-ops/role-activation-and-90-day-sponsor-playbook-2026
- /confluence/people-ops/structured-onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026

Appendix: example email to sponsor (copy)
Subject: Intro & first 30 days — [New Manager name]

Hi [Sponsor name],

Thanks for agreeing to sponsor [New Manager name]. Quick context: they start on [date]. My ask for the first 30 days: weekly 60-minute office hours, review of the 30-day plan before submission, and one shadowed coaching session. I’ve attached the 30-day plan template and the sponsor checklist. Can you confirm availability for weekly office hours?

Thanks,
People Ops

End of document.
